messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Lacuna Health integration roadmap & open technical asks

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the 45m call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so the team has a single place to reference. I focused this on product fit and the integration pieces you raised.

Key pain & goals (as we heard them)
- High false-positive rate in clinician triage summaries — want improved precision without increasing latency.
- Need deterministic, auditable outputs for regulatory review (structured fields + provenance).
- Keep endpoint latency under 350ms P95 for single-doc inference at expected traffic.
- Tight cost targets for inference; prefer a hybrid approach (hosted + dedicated capacity for peak windows).

Product/technical fit notes
- You liked the idea of using embeddings + reranking for candidate document retrieval. We recommended a 2-stage pipeline: dense retrieval -> small reranker model served by Redwood (multi-pass).
- SDK/function-calling: your product needs structured field extraction (JSON outputs) and the ability to call back to your orchestration layer with validated fields. We flagged Redwood function-calling + structured-output templates as a match.
- Streaming: for long notes, we suggested streaming token responses for progressive UI while applying prefix caching to reduce costs and latency.
- Quantization/instance sizing: initial POC on a8x for reranker and g5-standard for retrieval; we'll refine after perf tests.

Open technical questions (action items for Lacuna)
- Sample volume & payload size: can you share a representative set (anonymized) for the top 2000 triage docs? (Priya indicated she can prepare)
- Required extraction schema: a concise JSON schema for the fields you must capture for compliance.
- Reliability SLOs for business hours / off hours (do you need 24/7 identical SLAs?).

Our next steps 
1) You provide sample dataset + extraction schema (Priya) — target by Tue 5/18.
2) Redwood to share a scoped POC plan (tech stack, timeline, success metrics) — I’ll send draft by Fri 5/14.
3) Schedule technical deep dive with engineering (30–45m) — suggested slots Mon 5/17 or Wed 5/19.

Attachments: lacuna_mvp_requirements.xlsx (outline you can fill), redwood-infer-api-proposal.pdf (high-level architecture & costs).

If anything above is wrong or missed, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll calendar the deep-dive once I get the sample data ETA.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Lacuna Health integration roadmap & open technical asks

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Volume: for triage the 2k/day number I gave is for active triage; monthly archive brings the dataset to ~1.2M docs. We’ll prioritize the 2k/day set for the POC.

2) Extraction schema: attaching a quick sketch inline below — the compliance team wants source_id, extracted_condition (enum), confidence_score (0-1), extracted_text_span, extractor_version, and audit_token. Is Redwood able to return extractor_version and audit_token with each response? We need immutable provenance.

3) Latency: the 350ms P95 is aspirational for single-doc loads; we can accept higher for batched bulk jobs if needed.

4) Security: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) in the hosted plan? We may need to move to Dedicated with KMS for PHI workflows.

We’ll share the anonymized sample set (2k) by Tue 5/18 — Priya will lead.

—Sanjay
VP Product, Lacuna Health

Sanjay —

Great — thanks for the notes and the schema requirements. Quick answers:

- extractor_version & audit_token: yes — we can surface both in the structured output envelope. The audit_token will be a request-scoped UUID tied to the invocation and included in logs for the Private/Dedicated customers; for hosted we can provide an immutable response id and full request metadata for review.
- KMS: supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted API can integrate with customer-managed keys via our KMS proxy in beta; I’ll confirm controls with security and call that out in the POC doc.
- Latency: we’ll target 350ms P95 for single-doc inference in the POC; plan includes a small reranker (<200M params) colocated with a retrieval layer to meet the bar.

Actioning next steps: I’ll produce the POC plan by EOD Fri 5/14 and include an initial cost estimate for both hosted + dedicated carving (with burst capacity).

Also looping in Marissa and Jasmine from our side to help with SOW and technical deep-dive scheduling. Marissa — can you own the SOW draft? Jasmine — could you join the deep-dive to review SDK/function-calling constraints?

Thanks,
Karthik
